name: Dievas
role: Sky god and highest deity of the Baltic pantheon
fun_fact: Dievas is also the ordinary Lithuanian word for God, so the Christian and the older sky god are hard to separate in the sources.

name: Velnias
role: Trickster, rival and shaper of the world's rough places
fun_fact: In the creation tales Velnias dives for the first earth and hides a piece in his mouth, which swells into hills and rocks.

name: Perkūnas
role: God of thunder, lightning, rain and the oak
fun_fact: The first spring thunder was a signal to begin the fields, and a perpetual fire burned for Perkūnas at Vilnius.

name: Saulė
role: Sun goddess and wife of the moon
fun_fact: In Lithuanian dainos Saulė is called mummy and Mėnulis daddy, a household pair whose quarrel explains day and night.

name: Mėnulis
role: Moon god and husband of the sun
fun_fact: The moon's waning was told as a punishment: Perkūnas cut the unfaithful Mėnulis in two, or Saulė struck him with a silver whip.

name: Jūratė
role: Sea goddess of the amber palace
fun_fact: The popular Jūratė is largely a literary figure, fixed by Maironis's ballad in Pavasario balsai rather than by an ancient text.

name: Kastytis
role: Young fisherman who loves the sea goddess
fun_fact: Kastytis is a mortal who crosses into the sea world, and his death is the price of that crossing in most tellings.

name: Eglė
role: Heroine who marries the serpent and becomes a spruce
fun_fact: Eglė's name is also the Lithuanian word for spruce, so her final transformation is hidden in her name from the start.

name: Žilvinas
role: Serpent husband and king beneath the sea
fun_fact: Žilvinas is summoned by a rhyme: come as white milk foam if alive, as black blood foam if dead.

name: Sovijus
role: First teacher of the funeral rites and traveller to the dead
fun_fact: Sovijus tested burial in the earth and in a tree before fire, and only the pyre let him sleep 'like a child in a cradle'.
